items.explanation_consistent: 해설이 정답·오답 판단과 일치하고 글자 참조가 맞으면 true

items.passage: There was so much truth in this that Mulrady checked a sigh as he gave the required permission, without saying that he had intended to remain. He could cook his own breakfast: he had done it before; and it would be something to occupy him. As to his dinner, perhaps he could go to the hotel at Rough-and-Ready. He worked on until the night had well advanced. Then, overcome with a certain restlessness that disturbed him, he was forced to put his books and papers away. It had begun to blow in fitful gusts, and occasionally the rain was driven softly across the panes like the passing of childish fingers. This disturbed him more than the monotony of silence, for he was not a nervous man.
items.question: Based on the text, which choice best describes Mulrady's relationship with the person who asked for permission?
options: He resents the person and is glad to be left alone at last.
He depends on the person for money and fears losing it.
He outranks the person yet quietly misses the person.
He barely knows the person and gives no thought to the request.
items.explanation: Mulrady는 '요청받은 허락'을 내주므로 상대보다 권한이 있는 위치에 있다. 그런데 그는 한숨을 참고, 자신이 남으려 했다는 말도 하지 않으며, 밤이 되자 침묵 속에서 불안을 느낀다. 이는 상대의 부재를 아쉬워함을 보여 주므로 C가 정답이다. 혼자 남아 기뻐하거나 돈 문제를 걱정하거나 무관심한 모습은 없으므로 A, B, D는 틀리다.

items.passage: The white mists were still curtseying to one another across wider spaces in the valley, and the dim light behind them grew slowly stronger. There was a scent of turf-smoke on the air from a fire which someone had lit under a bank a little way down the hill. The very strokes of old Dan Heron’s hammer continued to come up in a faint rap-tap from the roadside, where he was breaking lumps of reddish sandstone; for Dan was so deaf that he applied himself to his tasks with abstracted concentration, and could not easily be interrupted. Evidently the news had not penetrated to him. A murmur of voices was passing to and fro in a knot of men gathered at a short distance. Pierce might have caught a sentence now and then.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “curtseying to one another” most nearly suggests that the mists are?
options: moving gently as if bowing to each other
clearing away suddenly before the sunrise
hiding the men gathered down the hill
thickening as the turf-smoke spreads
items.explanation: 'curtseying'은 무릎을 굽혀 인사하는 동작으로, 안개가 골짜기에서 서로를 향해 부드럽게 움직이는 모습을 의인화한다. 이어지는 문장에서 빛이 '천천히' 강해진다는 묘사도 느리고 고요한 아침 분위기를 뒷받침한다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 '갑자기' 걷힌다는 점, C와 D는 사람을 숨기거나 연기로 짙어진다는 근거가 없다는 점에서 틀리다.

items.passage: I chronicle wild doings in this place, and have no time for the sweets of love long denied. But strange as the bridal had been, so the nuptials were strange, one like the other played to a steel undertone. When Richard had his Jehane, at first he could not enjoy her. He rode away with her like a storm; the way was long, the pace furious. Not a word had passed between them, at least not a reasoned word. Once or twice at first he leaned forward over her shoulder and set his cheek to her glowing cheek.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “played to a steel undertone” most nearly suggests that the marriage had?
options: a cheerful music that filled the wedding feast
an underlying harshness running beneath it
a display of wealth in the couple's armor
a quiet sadness felt only by the narrator
items.explanation: 'steel undertone'은 결혼 밑에 깔린 차갑고 거친 기운을 음악 비유로 표현한 것이다. 리처드가 신부를 '폭풍처럼' 데려가고 속도가 '맹렬했으며' 제대로 된 말 한마디 없었다는 묘사가 이를 뒷받침한다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A의 즐거운 음악, C의 부의 과시, D의 화자만의 슬픔은 지문 근거가 없다.

items.passage:
I brought my doom upon myself,
And there I was upon the shelf
In melancholy.
Why, say you, did I go at all?
I once met Chloris at a ball,
And in my folly
I went and suffered all this pain
In hopes to see her once again.

Of strawberries a pound at least
I ate, and made myself a beast
With tea and sherry;
And raspberries I ate and trembled,
Until I felt that I resembled
Myself a berry,
But 'twas the berry that at school
We used to call a gooseberry fool.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “upon the shelf” most nearly suggests that the speaker was?
options: proudly displayed for everyone to admire him
busily serving food to the other guests
set aside and ignored by those around him
safely hidden from the woman he loved
items.explanation: 'upon the shelf'는 선반 위에 올려진 물건처럼 쓰이지 않고 밀려나 있는 상태를 뜻한다. 바로 뒤의 'In melancholy'와 스스로 '파멸'을 불렀다는 첫 줄이 화자가 무도회에서 소외되어 우울했음을 보여 준다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A는 감탄의 대상이라는 점, B는 음식을 대접했다는 점, D는 클로리스를 다시 보려고 갔다는 내용과 맞지 않아 틀리다.

items.passage:
On one hand we see an enormous increase in the brain power of the people--a multitude able to think, eager to think, not to be prevented from thinking, where only two or three generations ago the thinking was done exclusively by the few. On the other hand we see the necessity for more thinking, for vigorous stirring-up of the minds of the masses, for more and more education. And, year by year, the stirring-up process increases. The evils of the present day are as old as the race, as old as ignorance, as old as human frailty. The good, the benefits, are new, entirely new.

The material and mental forces of modern civilization have already wrought wonders.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “vigorous stirring-up of the minds of the masses” most nearly suggests a need for?
options: a violent disturbance that threatens order
a blending of all classes into one group
a confusion that stops people from thinking
an energetic effort to awaken thinking
items.explanation: 'stirring-up'은 휘저어 깨우는 동작으로, 대중의 정신을 활발히 일깨우는 일을 비유한다. 같은 문장에서 이것이 '더 많은 사고'와 '더 많은 교육'의 필요와 나란히 제시되고, 앞 문장도 생각하려는 대중의 증가를 말한다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A의 폭력적 혼란, B의 계층 혼합, C의 사고 마비는 교육을 긍정하는 글의 흐름과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: The mystical element in him was for ever reaching out in search of some Divine essence in the world. He was not in search at any time of personal relations. He attracted more affection than he ever gave; he rejoiced its sympathy and kindred companionship as a flower rejoices in sunshine; but I think he had little taste of the baffled suffering which accompanies all deep human passion. He once wrote "God has preserved me extraordinarily from intimacies with others. He has done this, not I. I have longed for intimacies and failed to win them." He had little of the pastoral spirit; I do not think that he yearned over unshepherded souls, or primarily desired to seek and save the lost. On the other hand he responded eagerly to any claim made to himself for help and guidance, and he was always eager not to chill or disappoint people who seemed to need him.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “as a flower rejoices in sunshine” most nearly suggests that the man felt?
options: a natural, easy pleasure in others' warmth
a constant struggle to earn people's affection
a fragile need that withered without company
a strong urge to seek out lonely, lost souls
items.explanation: 꽃이 햇빛을 즐기듯이라는 직유는 그가 타인의 공감을 애쓰지 않고 자연스럽게 즐겼음을 뜻한다. 같은 문장에서 그는 '준 것보다 많은 애정을 받았고' 깊은 열정의 고통은 거의 몰랐다고 하여 이를 뒷받침한다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 애정을 얻으려 애썼다는 점, C는 그가 개인적 관계를 찾지 않았다는 점, D는 길 잃은 영혼을 찾지 않았다는 서술과 어긋난다.

items.passage: The description of the forest was a description of the wood where she had first met Harcourt; the charm of it returned, until she almost seemed to again inhale its balsamic freshness in the pages before her. Now, as then, her youth came back with the same longing and regret. But more bewildering than all, it was herself that moved there, painted with the loving hand of the narrator. For the first time she experienced the delicious flattery of seeing herself as only a lover could see her. The smallest detail of her costume was suggested with an accuracy that pleasantly thrilled her feminine sense.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone in the text?
options: It moves from wistful remembrance to pleased surprise at her portrayal.
It moves from amused detachment to bitter anger at the narrator.
It moves from fearful suspicion to calm acceptance of Harcourt's absence.
It moves from careful analysis to boredom with the book's details.
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 그녀는 하코트를 처음 만난 숲을 떠올리며 '그리움과 후회'를 느낀다. 그러나 'But more bewildering than all' 이후 자신이 연인의 눈으로 그려졌음을 깨닫고 '달콤한 아첨'과 즐거운 전율을 느낀다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B의 분노, C의 의심, D의 지루함은 지문에 나타나지 않는다.

items.passage:
Miss Field won the first and third, her antagonist contenting himself with the second. It had always been so, and for ten years she had taken a childish delight in her skill. "My dear Doctor," she often said, "it takes a woman of brains to play chess."

"It does, indeed," he invariably answered, with an air of gallantry. Once he had been indiscreet and had won all three games, but that was in the beginning and it had never happened since.

When the clock struck ten, he looked at his heavy, old-fashioned silver watch with apparent surprise. "I had no idea it was so late," he said.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone in the text?
options: From bitter rivalry to warm reconciliation between the two players.
From Miss Field's pride to gentle irony about the Doctor's losses.
From cheerful conversation to sudden alarm at the lateness of the hour.
From solemn reflection to open mockery of Miss Field's chess skill.
items.explanation: 처음에는 필드 양이 체스 실력을 '어린아이처럼' 기뻐하는 모습이 그려진다. 그러나 박사가 한 번 '경솔하게' 세 판을 다 이긴 뒤 다시는 그런 일이 없었다는 서술에서 그가 일부러 져 준다는 은근한 아이러니가 드러난다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A의 원한, C의 놀람, D의 공개적 조롱은 근거가 없다.

items.passage: The drainage has been rendered better, and the fearful odours that met you at every turn have disappeared. The poor are indolent, dirty, thriftless, and ill-housed; but that does not much matter, as most of their lives are passed in the open air. The convents are suppressed, the schoolmaster is abroad, and they may grow better as the years roll by, and Italy, as a nation, once more becomes great and renowned. But a good deal has yet to be done. I heard of things to be seen in Naples of the most disgraceful and disgusting character.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone in the text?
options: From harsh condemnation to full satisfaction with Naples' progress.
From playful humor to deep grief over the suffering of the city's poor.
From measured hope about reforms to sharp disapproval of what remains.
From detached description to warm praise for Italy's former glory.
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 화자는 배수 개선, 학교 교육 등을 들며 이탈리아가 '나아질 수도 있다'고 조심스럽게 기대한다. 그러나 'But a good deal has yet to be done' 이후 '수치스럽고 역겨운' 일들을 언급하며 비판적 어조로 바뀐다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A는 순서가 반대이고, B의 슬픔과 D의 과거 찬양은 지문 근거가 없다.

items.passage: The high-priced quartet has never been relied upon, the chorus choir being preferred, not merely for its own singing, but because it served best in leading the congregation, and that was the thing ever kept in mind. Mr. Beecher loved the old-fashioned hymns, though he had also a hearty welcome for new ones, and he was never satisfied unless he got everybody to singing. I have often seen him jump up from his chair right in the middle of a hymn and hold up his hand for silence. "You are not singing this hymn right," he would say. "Sing it with more spirit, and let everybody sing."
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone in the text?
options: From fond praise of Beecher to sharp criticism of his strict methods.
From excitement about new hymns to regret over losing the old ones.
From formal complaint about the choir to amused approval of the quartet.
From calm explanation to a lively scene of Beecher in action.
items.explanation: 앞부분은 비싼 사중창단 대신 합창단을 둔 이유를 차분히 설명한다. 이후 'I have often seen him jump up' 부분부터 비처가 찬송 도중 벌떡 일어나 손을 들고 직접 외치는 생생한 장면으로 바뀐다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A의 비판, B의 후회, C의 사중창단 칭찬은 지문 내용과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage:
The loss of her son struck the final blow to Mrs. Hale's already declining health, and a severe attack of fever, which for some time threatened her life, left her totally blind. She arose from her bed of sickness, a sadder but a wiser woman, confessing the folly and weakness of which she had been guilty in her treatment of Tom.

She was no longer able to work for herself, and her friends advised her to go into the workhouse. But the poor woman clung so fondly to her old home, every corner of which was familiar to her, and into every room of which she could soon grope her way by means of a stick, that Sir Herbert, to whom the cottage belonged, consented to her staying in it as long as she liked.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It describes a misfortune that blinds Mrs. Hale and how she keeps her home.
It recounts Tom's return home and then describes Mrs. Hale's joyful recovery.
It compares the cottage with the workhouse and then argues for the workhouse.
It introduces Sir Herbert as a landlord and then lists the rules of his cottages.
items.explanation: 첫 단락은 아들을 잃은 충격과 열병으로 헤일 부인이 시력을 잃는 불행을 서술한다. 둘째 단락은 일할 수 없게 된 그녀가 구빈원 대신 익숙한 집에 계속 머물게 되는 과정을 보여 준다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 톰의 귀환이 없고, C는 구빈원을 옹호하지 않으며, D는 허버트 경이 잠깐 언급될 뿐이라 틀리다.

items.passage:
Tam would have come into it almost intact. He might have been able to educate himself while he was yet young, to spare himself many a drudging day and weary night.

But looking back calmly over the gulf of years, with the mountains of difficulty well past, the man decided it was better as it had been. He had profited by the warfare he had undergone--it had made twice the man of him that he might have been otherwise. It was more honourable to have hewed out the fortune which he honestly thought so great and enviable, than to have derived even a part of it from the gift of another.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It lists Tam's many hardships and then blames another person for them.
It imagines an easier past for Tam and then why he prefers his own.
It describes Tam's present fortune and then predicts how he will spend it.
It recounts a quarrel over a gift and then describes how it was settled.
items.explanation: 첫 단락은 탐이 재산을 물려받았다면 일찍 교육받고 고생을 덜 했을 것이라는 가정을 제시한다. 둘째 단락은 'But' 이후 그가 지난 투쟁이 자신을 두 배의 사람으로 만들었으므로 실제 삶이 더 나았다고 결론짓는다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A의 남 탓, C의 미래 예측, D의 다툼은 지문에 없다.

items.passage:
Be sure that every motive which comes not from the single eye; every motive which springs from self; is by its very essence unheroic, let it look as gaudy or as beneficent as it may.

But I cannot go so far as to say the same of the love of approbation--the desire for the love and respect of our fellow-men.

That must not be excluded from the list of heroic motives. I know that it is, or may be proved to be, by victorious analysis, an emotion common to us and the lower animals. And yet no man excludes it less than that true hero, St. Paul.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It praises St. Paul's heroism and then lists the motives he rejected.
It defines heroism and then argues that no human motive is heroic.
It rejects selfish motives and then defends one, love of approval.
It describes animal emotions and then contrasts them with human habits.
items.explanation: 글은 먼저 자기에게서 나온 동기는 본질적으로 영웅적이지 않다고 단언한다. 이어 'But' 이후 인정받고 싶은 욕구만은 예외라고 하며 반론을 인정한 뒤 성 바울을 예로 들어 옹호한다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A는 성 바울이 마지막 예시일 뿐이고, B는 예외를 인정하는 내용과 어긋나며, D는 동물 감정이 반론의 일부로만 언급되어 틀리다.

items.passage: Certainly there is no nobler field for human effort than the insurance line of business--especially accident insurance. Ever since I have been a director in an accident-insurance company I have felt that I am a better man. Life has seemed more precious. Accidents have assumed a kindlier aspect. Distressing special providences have lost half their horror. I look upon a cripple now with affectionate interest--as an advertisement. I do not seem to care for poetry any more. I do not care for politics--even agriculture does not excite me.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward accident insurance?
options: Reluctant acceptance of a dull but necessary occupation
Exaggerated enthusiasm that reveals a comically narrow outlook
Quiet regret about having given up his former love of poetry and politics
Sincere sympathy for the people injured in accidents
items.explanation: 화자는 보험업을 '가장 고귀한 분야'라 부르며 지나치게 열광한다. 그러나 장애인을 '광고'로 본다거나 시와 정치에 더는 관심이 없다고 말하는 대목에서 그 열광이 우스꽝스럽게 편협함이 드러난다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A의 마지못한 수용, C의 후회, D의 진심 어린 동정은 모두 지문의 어조와 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: Intending to engrave the name later in the afternoon, I wrote it down in my order-book, and asked the lady for her address, so that I might send the chain to her the next day. But, no; she would not leave it. She must have the name engraved at once, right away, and must put the necklace herself on her little daughter. She would wait. Ah, how it all comes back to me! Well, I wished to obey the lady, and so set to work. But I saw immediately there was not space enough for the whole name. She was very sorry, poor lady, and then she said I should put on the two letters D. R. There they are, you see, my own work--you see that? And she paid me, and locked the chain on the baby's neck again--ah me! it is so strange!--and she went away.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward the memory of the lady's visit?
options: Annoyance at the lady's impatient demands
Pride in having finished the engraving so quickly and skillfully
Wistful emotion at how vividly the moment returns
Doubt about whether the visit really happened
items.explanation: 화자는 '아, 모든 것이 되살아난다!'라고 외치며 그 기억에 감정적으로 반응한다. 또 '아 이런! 참 이상하다!'라는 탄식에서 아련하고 감상적인 태도가 드러난다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. 화자는 부인의 요구에 따르고자 했으므로 A의 짜증은 맞지 않고, 자신의 솜씨를 보여 주긴 하지만 B처럼 빠른 작업을 자랑하는 것은 아니며, D의 의심도 없다.

items.passage:
Was it last Autumn only, when I stood
At the field’s edge, and watched the red glow creep
Among the leaves, and saw the swift flame sweep
From spruce to hemlock, till the living wood
Became a devastated solitude?
For now, behold, old seeds, long years asleep,
Wake; and a legion of young birches leap
To life, and tell the ashes life is good.
O Love of long ago, when this mad fire
Is over, and the ruins of my soul
With the Spring wind the old quest would resume,--
When age knocks at the inn of youth’s desire,
Shall the new growth, now worthier of the goal,
Find still untenanted the chosen room?
items.question: Which choice best describes the speaker's attitude toward the future of an old love?
options: Bitter certainty that the fire has destroyed the old love beyond any hope
Calm indifference toward the ruins left by the fire
Joyful confidence that youth can be fully restored
Hopeful uncertainty about whether that love will still welcome him
items.explanation: 화자는 불탄 숲에서 어린 자작나무가 다시 솟아나는 모습을 보며 생명이 좋다는 희망을 본다. 그러나 마지막에 새로 자란 자신이 그 '방'을 여전히 비어 있는 채로 찾을지 질문으로 끝맺어 불확실함을 드러낸다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 재생의 희망과 어긋나고, B의 무관심이나 C의 확신은 질문형 결말과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: I planted myself against the rock, and he started cautiously up the wall. Looking down the glare front of ice, it was not pleasant to consider at what velocity a slip would send me to the bottom, or at what angle, and to what probable depth, I should be projected into the ice-water. Indeed, the idea of such a sudden bath was so annoying that I lifted my eyes toward my companion. He reached my farthest point without great difficulty, and made a bold spring for the crack, reaching it without an inch to spare, and holding on wholly by his fingers.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward his position below the ice wall?
options: Calm confidence that a fall would cause no harm
Uneasy awareness of the danger a slip would bring
Open resentment toward his companion for the climb
Playful excitement about a sudden bath in ice-water
items.explanation: 화자는 미끄러지면 어떤 속도로 떨어질지 생각하는 것이 '유쾌하지 않았다'고 말한다. 또 얼음물에 빠질 생각이 너무 싫어 동료 쪽으로 눈을 들었다고 서술한다. 따라서 B처럼 위험을 불안하게 의식하는 태도다. A의 자신감, C의 원망, D의 장난스러운 흥분은 모두 지문과 어긋난다.

items.passage: Otto, then, had never penetrated into a character whose reserve was so like his own that he could not understand it. He loved his young wife, and kissed her; and he fancied, like so many men, that his consciousness of loving her was sufficient for all her wants. As for her position in the house, in the family, if it was uncomfortable, could he help that? Was not he himself weighed down by his difficulties, his responsibilities, the worry of universal deepening displeasure? What were the pinpricks she complained of compared to his wounds?
items.question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
options: To praise Otto for patiently enduring the many difficulties and responsibilities he faces
To describe the household duties that Otto's wife neglects
To show that Otto's wife openly complains to the whole family
To reveal how Otto's self-absorption keeps him from understanding his wife
items.explanation: 서술자는 오토가 아내의 성격을 꿰뚫어 본 적이 없으며 사랑한다는 자각만으로 충분하다고 착각한다고 말한다. 이어 자신의 상처에 비하면 아내의 불만은 바늘에 찔린 정도라고 여기는 오토의 생각을 보여 준다. 따라서 D처럼 자기중심성이 아내 이해를 막는다는 점을 드러내는 것이 목적이다. A의 칭찬, B의 집안일, C의 공개적 불평은 지문의 초점이 아니다.

items.passage:
The secret of thriving is thrift; saving of force; to get as much work as possible done with the least expenditure of power, the least jar and obstruction, the least wear and tear.

And the secret of thrift is knowledge. In proportion as you know the laws and nature of a subject, you will be able to work at it easily, surely, rapidly, successfully; instead of wasting your money or your energies in mistaken schemes, irregular efforts, which end in disappointment and exhaustion.

The secret of thrift, I say, is knowledge. The more you know, the more you can save yourself and that which belongs to you; and can do more work with less effort.
items.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Knowledge allows people to work efficiently and avoid wasted effort.
Saving money matters far more than gaining knowledge about any particular subject.
Hard work without rest eventually leads to exhaustion.
Most schemes for thriving end in disappointment.
items.explanation: 글쓴이는 번영의 비결이 힘을 아끼는 절약이라고 한 뒤, 절약의 비결은 지식이라고 거듭 말한다. 많이 알수록 적은 노력으로 더 많은 일을 할 수 있다고 정리한다. 따라서 A가 요지다. B는 지식과 돈의 우선순위를 뒤집었고, C와 D는 잘못된 시도의 결과를 언급한 일부 내용을 과장한 것이다.

## 문항
### lit40-easy-03-040 — skill inferences · 유형 relationship_between_characters
[지문]
There was so much truth in this that Mulrady checked a sigh as he gave the required permission, without saying that he had intended to remain. He could cook his own breakfast: he had done it before; and it would be something to occupy him. As to his dinner, perhaps he could go to the hotel at Rough-and-Ready. He worked on until the night had well advanced. Then, overcome with a certain restlessness that disturbed him, he was forced to put his books and papers away. It had begun to blow in fitful gusts, and occasionally the rain was driven softly across the panes like the passing of childish fingers. This disturbed him more than the monotony of silence, for he was not a nervous man.

[질문] Based on the text, which choice best describes Mulrady's relationship with the person who asked for permission?
A) He resents the person and is glad to be left alone at last.
B) He depends on the person for money and fears losing it.
C) He outranks the person yet quietly misses the person.
D) He barely knows the person and gives no thought to the request.

[표시된 정답] C
[해설]
Mulrady는 '요청받은 허락'을 내주므로 상대보다 권한이 있는 위치에 있다. 그런데 그는 한숨을 참고, 자신이 남으려 했다는 말도 하지 않으며, 밤이 되자 침묵 속에서 불안을 느낀다. 이는 상대의 부재를 아쉬워함을 보여 주므로 C가 정답이다. 혼자 남아 기뻐하거나 돈 문제를 걱정하거나 무관심한 모습은 없으므로 A, B, D는 틀리다.
### lit40-easy-03-042 — skill words_in_context · 유형 figurative_language
[지문]
The white mists were still curtseying to one another across wider spaces in the valley, and the dim light behind them grew slowly stronger. There was a scent of turf-smoke on the air from a fire which someone had lit under a bank a little way down the hill. The very strokes of old Dan Heron’s hammer continued to come up in a faint rap-tap from the roadside, where he was breaking lumps of reddish sandstone; for Dan was so deaf that he applied himself to his tasks with abstracted concentration, and could not easily be interrupted. Evidently the news had not penetrated to him. A murmur of voices was passing to and fro in a knot of men gathered at a short distance. Pierce might have caught a sentence now and then.

[질문] As used in the text, the phrase “curtseying to one another” most nearly suggests that the mists are?
A) moving gently as if bowing to each other
B) clearing away suddenly before the sunrise
C) hiding the men gathered down the hill
D) thickening as the turf-smoke spreads

[표시된 정답] A
[해설]
'curtseying'은 무릎을 굽혀 인사하는 동작으로, 안개가 골짜기에서 서로를 향해 부드럽게 움직이는 모습을 의인화한다. 이어지는 문장에서 빛이 '천천히' 강해진다는 묘사도 느리고 고요한 아침 분위기를 뒷받침한다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 '갑자기' 걷힌다는 점, C와 D는 사람을 숨기거나 연기로 짙어진다는 근거가 없다는 점에서 틀리다.
### lit40-easy-03-043 — skill words_in_context · 유형 figurative_language
[지문]
I chronicle wild doings in this place, and have no time for the sweets of love long denied. But strange as the bridal had been, so the nuptials were strange, one like the other played to a steel undertone. When Richard had his Jehane, at first he could not enjoy her. He rode away with her like a storm; the way was long, the pace furious. Not a word had passed between them, at least not a reasoned word. Once or twice at first he leaned forward over her shoulder and set his cheek to her glowing cheek.

[질문] As used in the text, the phrase “played to a steel undertone” most nearly suggests that the marriage had?
A) a cheerful music that filled the wedding feast
B) an underlying harshness running beneath it
C) a display of wealth in the couple's armor
D) a quiet sadness felt only by the narrator

[표시된 정답] B
[해설]
'steel undertone'은 결혼 밑에 깔린 차갑고 거친 기운을 음악 비유로 표현한 것이다. 리처드가 신부를 '폭풍처럼' 데려가고 속도가 '맹렬했으며' 제대로 된 말 한마디 없었다는 묘사가 이를 뒷받침한다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A의 즐거운 음악, C의 부의 과시, D의 화자만의 슬픔은 지문 근거가 없다.
### lit40-easy-03-044 — skill words_in_context · 유형 figurative_language
[지문]
I brought my doom upon myself,
And there I was upon the shelf
In melancholy.
Why, say you, did I go at all?
I once met Chloris at a ball,
And in my folly
I went and suffered all this pain
In hopes to see her once again.

Of strawberries a pound at least
I ate, and made myself a beast
With tea and sherry;
And raspberries I ate and trembled,
Until I felt that I resembled
Myself a berry,
But 'twas the berry that at school
We used to call a gooseberry fool.

[질문] As used in the text, the phrase “upon the shelf” most nearly suggests that the speaker was?
A) proudly displayed for everyone to admire him
B) busily serving food to the other guests
C) set aside and ignored by those around him
D) safely hidden from the woman he loved

[표시된 정답] C
[해설]
'upon the shelf'는 선반 위에 올려진 물건처럼 쓰이지 않고 밀려나 있는 상태를 뜻한다. 바로 뒤의 'In melancholy'와 스스로 '파멸'을 불렀다는 첫 줄이 화자가 무도회에서 소외되어 우울했음을 보여 준다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A는 감탄의 대상이라는 점, B는 음식을 대접했다는 점, D는 클로리스를 다시 보려고 갔다는 내용과 맞지 않아 틀리다.
### lit40-easy-03-045 — skill words_in_context · 유형 figurative_language
[지문]
On one hand we see an enormous increase in the brain power of the people--a multitude able to think, eager to think, not to be prevented from thinking, where only two or three generations ago the thinking was done exclusively by the few. On the other hand we see the necessity for more thinking, for vigorous stirring-up of the minds of the masses, for more and more education. And, year by year, the stirring-up process increases. The evils of the present day are as old as the race, as old as ignorance, as old as human frailty. The good, the benefits, are new, entirely new.

The material and mental forces of modern civilization have already wrought wonders.

[질문] As used in the text, the phrase “vigorous stirring-up of the minds of the masses” most nearly suggests a need for?
A) a violent disturbance that threatens order
B) a blending of all classes into one group
C) a confusion that stops people from thinking
D) an energetic effort to awaken thinking

[표시된 정답] D
[해설]
'stirring-up'은 휘저어 깨우는 동작으로, 대중의 정신을 활발히 일깨우는 일을 비유한다. 같은 문장에서 이것이 '더 많은 사고'와 '더 많은 교육'의 필요와 나란히 제시되고, 앞 문장도 생각하려는 대중의 증가를 말한다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A의 폭력적 혼란, B의 계층 혼합, C의 사고 마비는 교육을 긍정하는 글의 흐름과 맞지 않는다.
### lit40-easy-03-046 — skill words_in_context · 유형 figurative_language
[지문]
The mystical element in him was for ever reaching out in search of some Divine essence in the world. He was not in search at any time of personal relations. He attracted more affection than he ever gave; he rejoiced its sympathy and kindred companionship as a flower rejoices in sunshine; but I think he had little taste of the baffled suffering which accompanies all deep human passion. He once wrote "God has preserved me extraordinarily from intimacies with others. He has done this, not I. I have longed for intimacies and failed to win them." He had little of the pastoral spirit; I do not think that he yearned over unshepherded souls, or primarily desired to seek and save the lost. On the other hand he responded eagerly to any claim made to himself for help and guidance, and he was always eager not to chill or disappoint people who seemed to need him.

[질문] As used in the text, the phrase “as a flower rejoices in sunshine” most nearly suggests that the man felt?
A) a natural, easy pleasure in others' warmth
B) a constant struggle to earn people's affection
C) a fragile need that withered without company
D) a strong urge to seek out lonely, lost souls

[표시된 정답] A
[해설]
꽃이 햇빛을 즐기듯이라는 직유는 그가 타인의 공감을 애쓰지 않고 자연스럽게 즐겼음을 뜻한다. 같은 문장에서 그는 '준 것보다 많은 애정을 받았고' 깊은 열정의 고통은 거의 몰랐다고 하여 이를 뒷받침한다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 애정을 얻으려 애썼다는 점, C는 그가 개인적 관계를 찾지 않았다는 점, D는 길 잃은 영혼을 찾지 않았다는 서술과 어긋난다.
### lit40-easy-03-052 — skill text_structure_purpose · 유형 tone_shift
[지문]
The description of the forest was a description of the wood where she had first met Harcourt; the charm of it returned, until she almost seemed to again inhale its balsamic freshness in the pages before her. Now, as then, her youth came back with the same longing and regret. But more bewildering than all, it was herself that moved there, painted with the loving hand of the narrator. For the first time she experienced the delicious flattery of seeing herself as only a lover could see her. The smallest detail of her costume was suggested with an accuracy that pleasantly thrilled her feminine sense.

[질문] Which choice best describes the shift in tone in the text?
A) It moves from wistful remembrance to pleased surprise at her portrayal.
B) It moves from amused detachment to bitter anger at the narrator.
C) It moves from fearful suspicion to calm acceptance of Harcourt's absence.
D) It moves from careful analysis to boredom with the book's details.

[표시된 정답] A
[해설]
앞부분에서 그녀는 하코트를 처음 만난 숲을 떠올리며 '그리움과 후회'를 느낀다. 그러나 'But more bewildering than all' 이후 자신이 연인의 눈으로 그려졌음을 깨닫고 '달콤한 아첨'과 즐거운 전율을 느낀다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B의 분노, C의 의심, D의 지루함은 지문에 나타나지 않는다.
### lit40-easy-03-053 — skill text_structure_purpose · 유형 tone_shift
[지문]
Miss Field won the first and third, her antagonist contenting himself with the second. It had always been so, and for ten years she had taken a childish delight in her skill. "My dear Doctor," she often said, "it takes a woman of brains to play chess."

"It does, indeed," he invariably answered, with an air of gallantry. Once he had been indiscreet and had won all three games, but that was in the beginning and it had never happened since.

When the clock struck ten, he looked at his heavy, old-fashioned silver watch with apparent surprise. "I had no idea it was so late," he said.

[질문] Which choice best describes the shift in tone in the text?
A) From bitter rivalry to warm reconciliation between the two players.
B) From Miss Field's pride to gentle irony about the Doctor's losses.
C) From cheerful conversation to sudden alarm at the lateness of the hour.
D) From solemn reflection to open mockery of Miss Field's chess skill.

[표시된 정답] B
[해설]
처음에는 필드 양이 체스 실력을 '어린아이처럼' 기뻐하는 모습이 그려진다. 그러나 박사가 한 번 '경솔하게' 세 판을 다 이긴 뒤 다시는 그런 일이 없었다는 서술에서 그가 일부러 져 준다는 은근한 아이러니가 드러난다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A의 원한, C의 놀람, D의 공개적 조롱은 근거가 없다.
### lit40-easy-03-054 — skill text_structure_purpose · 유형 tone_shift
[지문]
The drainage has been rendered better, and the fearful odours that met you at every turn have disappeared. The poor are indolent, dirty, thriftless, and ill-housed; but that does not much matter, as most of their lives are passed in the open air. The convents are suppressed, the schoolmaster is abroad, and they may grow better as the years roll by, and Italy, as a nation, once more becomes great and renowned. But a good deal has yet to be done. I heard of things to be seen in Naples of the most disgraceful and disgusting character.

[질문] Which choice best describes the shift in tone in the text?
A) From harsh condemnation to full satisfaction with Naples' progress.
B) From playful humor to deep grief over the suffering of the city's poor.
C) From measured hope about reforms to sharp disapproval of what remains.
D) From detached description to warm praise for Italy's former glory.

[표시된 정답] C
[해설]
앞부분에서 화자는 배수 개선, 학교 교육 등을 들며 이탈리아가 '나아질 수도 있다'고 조심스럽게 기대한다. 그러나 'But a good deal has yet to be done' 이후 '수치스럽고 역겨운' 일들을 언급하며 비판적 어조로 바뀐다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A는 순서가 반대이고, B의 슬픔과 D의 과거 찬양은 지문 근거가 없다.
### lit40-easy-03-055 — skill text_structure_purpose · 유형 tone_shift
[지문]
The high-priced quartet has never been relied upon, the chorus choir being preferred, not merely for its own singing, but because it served best in leading the congregation, and that was the thing ever kept in mind. Mr. Beecher loved the old-fashioned hymns, though he had also a hearty welcome for new ones, and he was never satisfied unless he got everybody to singing. I have often seen him jump up from his chair right in the middle of a hymn and hold up his hand for silence. "You are not singing this hymn right," he would say. "Sing it with more spirit, and let everybody sing."

[질문] Which choice best describes the shift in tone in the text?
A) From fond praise of Beecher to sharp criticism of his strict methods.
B) From excitement about new hymns to regret over losing the old ones.
C) From formal complaint about the choir to amused approval of the quartet.
D) From calm explanation to a lively scene of Beecher in action.

[표시된 정답] D
[해설]
앞부분은 비싼 사중창단 대신 합창단을 둔 이유를 차분히 설명한다. 이후 'I have often seen him jump up' 부분부터 비처가 찬송 도중 벌떡 일어나 손을 들고 직접 외치는 생생한 장면으로 바뀐다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A의 비판, B의 후회, C의 사중창단 칭찬은 지문 내용과 맞지 않는다.
### lit40-easy-03-056 — skill text_structure_purpose · 유형 text_structure
[지문]
The loss of her son struck the final blow to Mrs. Hale's already declining health, and a severe attack of fever, which for some time threatened her life, left her totally blind. She arose from her bed of sickness, a sadder but a wiser woman, confessing the folly and weakness of which she had been guilty in her treatment of Tom.

She was no longer able to work for herself, and her friends advised her to go into the workhouse. But the poor woman clung so fondly to her old home, every corner of which was familiar to her, and into every room of which she could soon grope her way by means of a stick, that Sir Herbert, to whom the cottage belonged, consented to her staying in it as long as she liked.

[질문] Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
A) It describes a misfortune that blinds Mrs. Hale and how she keeps her home.
B) It recounts Tom's return home and then describes Mrs. Hale's joyful recovery.
C) It compares the cottage with the workhouse and then argues for the workhouse.
D) It introduces Sir Herbert as a landlord and then lists the rules of his cottages.

[표시된 정답] A
[해설]
첫 단락은 아들을 잃은 충격과 열병으로 헤일 부인이 시력을 잃는 불행을 서술한다. 둘째 단락은 일할 수 없게 된 그녀가 구빈원 대신 익숙한 집에 계속 머물게 되는 과정을 보여 준다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 톰의 귀환이 없고, C는 구빈원을 옹호하지 않으며, D는 허버트 경이 잠깐 언급될 뿐이라 틀리다.
### lit40-easy-03-057 — skill text_structure_purpose · 유형 text_structure
[지문]
Tam would have come into it almost intact. He might have been able to educate himself while he was yet young, to spare himself many a drudging day and weary night.

But looking back calmly over the gulf of years, with the mountains of difficulty well past, the man decided it was better as it had been. He had profited by the warfare he had undergone--it had made twice the man of him that he might have been otherwise. It was more honourable to have hewed out the fortune which he honestly thought so great and enviable, than to have derived even a part of it from the gift of another.

[질문] Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
A) It lists Tam's many hardships and then blames another person for them.
B) It imagines an easier past for Tam and then why he prefers his own.
C) It describes Tam's present fortune and then predicts how he will spend it.
D) It recounts a quarrel over a gift and then describes how it was settled.

[표시된 정답] B
[해설]
첫 단락은 탐이 재산을 물려받았다면 일찍 교육받고 고생을 덜 했을 것이라는 가정을 제시한다. 둘째 단락은 'But' 이후 그가 지난 투쟁이 자신을 두 배의 사람으로 만들었으므로 실제 삶이 더 나았다고 결론짓는다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A의 남 탓, C의 미래 예측, D의 다툼은 지문에 없다.
### lit40-easy-03-058 — skill text_structure_purpose · 유형 text_structure
[지문]
Be sure that every motive which comes not from the single eye; every motive which springs from self; is by its very essence unheroic, let it look as gaudy or as beneficent as it may.

But I cannot go so far as to say the same of the love of approbation--the desire for the love and respect of our fellow-men.

That must not be excluded from the list of heroic motives. I know that it is, or may be proved to be, by victorious analysis, an emotion common to us and the lower animals. And yet no man excludes it less than that true hero, St. Paul.

[질문] Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
A) It praises St. Paul's heroism and then lists the motives he rejected.
B) It defines heroism and then argues that no human motive is heroic.
C) It rejects selfish motives and then defends one, love of approval.
D) It describes animal emotions and then contrasts them with human habits.

[표시된 정답] C
[해설]
글은 먼저 자기에게서 나온 동기는 본질적으로 영웅적이지 않다고 단언한다. 이어 'But' 이후 인정받고 싶은 욕구만은 예외라고 하며 반론을 인정한 뒤 성 바울을 예로 들어 옹호한다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A는 성 바울이 마지막 예시일 뿐이고, B는 예외를 인정하는 내용과 어긋나며, D는 동물 감정이 반론의 일부로만 언급되어 틀리다.
### lit40-easy-03-062 — skill central_ideas_details · 유형 narrator_attitude
[지문]
Certainly there is no nobler field for human effort than the insurance line of business--especially accident insurance. Ever since I have been a director in an accident-insurance company I have felt that I am a better man. Life has seemed more precious. Accidents have assumed a kindlier aspect. Distressing special providences have lost half their horror. I look upon a cripple now with affectionate interest--as an advertisement. I do not seem to care for poetry any more. I do not care for politics--even agriculture does not excite me.

[질문] Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward accident insurance?
A) Reluctant acceptance of a dull but necessary occupation
B) Exaggerated enthusiasm that reveals a comically narrow outlook
C) Quiet regret about having given up his former love of poetry and politics
D) Sincere sympathy for the people injured in accidents

[표시된 정답] B
[해설]
화자는 보험업을 '가장 고귀한 분야'라 부르며 지나치게 열광한다. 그러나 장애인을 '광고'로 본다거나 시와 정치에 더는 관심이 없다고 말하는 대목에서 그 열광이 우스꽝스럽게 편협함이 드러난다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A의 마지못한 수용, C의 후회, D의 진심 어린 동정은 모두 지문의 어조와 맞지 않는다.
### lit40-easy-03-063 — skill central_ideas_details · 유형 narrator_attitude
[지문]
Intending to engrave the name later in the afternoon, I wrote it down in my order-book, and asked the lady for her address, so that I might send the chain to her the next day. But, no; she would not leave it. She must have the name engraved at once, right away, and must put the necklace herself on her little daughter. She would wait. Ah, how it all comes back to me! Well, I wished to obey the lady, and so set to work. But I saw immediately there was not space enough for the whole name. She was very sorry, poor lady, and then she said I should put on the two letters D. R. There they are, you see, my own work--you see that? And she paid me, and locked the chain on the baby's neck again--ah me! it is so strange!--and she went away.

[질문] Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward the memory of the lady's visit?
A) Annoyance at the lady's impatient demands
B) Pride in having finished the engraving so quickly and skillfully
C) Wistful emotion at how vividly the moment returns
D) Doubt about whether the visit really happened

[표시된 정답] C
[해설]
화자는 '아, 모든 것이 되살아난다!'라고 외치며 그 기억에 감정적으로 반응한다. 또 '아 이런! 참 이상하다!'라는 탄식에서 아련하고 감상적인 태도가 드러난다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. 화자는 부인의 요구에 따르고자 했으므로 A의 짜증은 맞지 않고, 자신의 솜씨를 보여 주긴 하지만 B처럼 빠른 작업을 자랑하는 것은 아니며, D의 의심도 없다.
### lit40-easy-03-064 — skill central_ideas_details · 유형 narrator_attitude
[지문]
Was it last Autumn only, when I stood
At the field’s edge, and watched the red glow creep
Among the leaves, and saw the swift flame sweep
From spruce to hemlock, till the living wood
Became a devastated solitude?
For now, behold, old seeds, long years asleep,
Wake; and a legion of young birches leap
To life, and tell the ashes life is good.
O Love of long ago, when this mad fire
Is over, and the ruins of my soul
With the Spring wind the old quest would resume,--
When age knocks at the inn of youth’s desire,
Shall the new growth, now worthier of the goal,
Find still untenanted the chosen room?

[질문] Which choice best describes the speaker's attitude toward the future of an old love?
A) Bitter certainty that the fire has destroyed the old love beyond any hope
B) Calm indifference toward the ruins left by the fire
C) Joyful confidence that youth can be fully restored
D) Hopeful uncertainty about whether that love will still welcome him

[표시된 정답] D
[해설]
화자는 불탄 숲에서 어린 자작나무가 다시 솟아나는 모습을 보며 생명이 좋다는 희망을 본다. 그러나 마지막에 새로 자란 자신이 그 '방'을 여전히 비어 있는 채로 찾을지 질문으로 끝맺어 불확실함을 드러낸다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 재생의 희망과 어긋나고, B의 무관심이나 C의 확신은 질문형 결말과 맞지 않는다.
### lit40-easy-03-066 — skill central_ideas_details · 유형 narrator_attitude

Indeed, the idea of such a sudden bath was so annoying that I lifted my eyes toward my companion. [질문] Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward his position below the ice wall?
A) Calm confidence that a fall would cause no harm

C) Open resentment toward his companion for the climb
D) Playful excitement about a sudden bath in ice-water

### lit40-easy-03-068 — skill central_ideas_details · 유형 main_idea_or_purpose
[지문]
Otto, then, had never penetrated into a character whose reserve was so like his own that he could not understand it. He loved his young wife, and kissed her; and he fancied, like so many men, that his consciousness of loving her was sufficient for all her wants. As for her position in the house, in the family, if it was uncomfortable, could he help that? Was not he himself weighed down by his difficulties, his responsibilities, the worry of universal deepening displeasure? What were the pinpricks she complained of compared to his wounds?

[질문] Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
A) To praise Otto for patiently enduring the many difficulties and responsibilities he faces
B) To describe the household duties that Otto's wife neglects
C) To show that Otto's wife openly complains to the whole family
D) To reveal how Otto's self-absorption keeps him from understanding his wife

[표시된 정답] D
[해설]
서술자는 오토가 아내의 성격을 꿰뚫어 본 적이 없으며 사랑한다는 자각만으로 충분하다고 착각한다고 말한다. 이어 자신의 상처에 비하면 아내의 불만은 바늘에 찔린 정도라고 여기는 오토의 생각을 보여 준다. 따라서 D처럼 자기중심성이 아내 이해를 막는다는 점을 드러내는 것이 목적이다. A의 칭찬, B의 집안일, C의 공개적 불평은 지문의 초점이 아니다.
### lit40-easy-03-069 — skill central_ideas_details · 유형 main_idea_or_purpose
[지문]
The secret of thriving is thrift; saving of force; to get as much work as possible done with the least expenditure of power, the least jar and obstruction, the least wear and tear.

And the secret of thrift is knowledge. In proportion as you know the laws and nature of a subject, you will be able to work at it easily, surely, rapidly, successfully; instead of wasting your money or your energies in mistaken schemes, irregular efforts, which end in disappointment and exhaustion.

The secret of thrift, I say, is knowledge. The more you know, the more you can save yourself and that which belongs to you; and can do more work with less effort.

[질문] Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
A) Knowledge allows people to work efficiently and avoid wasted effort.
B) Saving money matters far more than gaining knowledge about any particular subject.
C) Hard work without rest eventually leads to exhaustion.
D) Most schemes for thriving end in disappointment.

[표시된 정답] A
[해설]
글쓴이는 번영의 비결이 힘을 아끼는 절약이라고 한 뒤, 절약의 비결은 지식이라고 거듭 말한다. 많이 알수록 적은 노력으로 더 많은 일을 할 수 있다고 정리한다. 따라서 A가 요지다. B는 지식과 돈의 우선순위를 뒤집었고, C와 D는 잘못된 시도의 결과를 언급한 일부 내용을 과장한 것이다.
